also: I don't go in for sports

evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.33.3: piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur
terms.comment: With the genitive of the thing. “It interests me” is mē tenet, it holds me: ille liber mē tenet, that book is interesting (Traupman 101); philosophiae studium mē tenet (Morgan–Owens).

terms.gloss: be interested in, be keen on (+ dative)
evidence: Traupman 101: mūsicae studeō, I am interested in music
Cic. Amic. 74: vēnandī aut pilae studiōsī

phrases.latin: omnis hīc aetās piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur
phrases.english: everyone here, young and old, is keen on fishing, sailing and swimming too

phrases.latin: suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur
phrases.english: for each of us is led most by his own interests

sources: Lewis & Short: studium · Lewis & Short: studeo · Lewis & Short: studiosus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. interest vb..
